title: IG artefact JSON-LD
summary: One JSON-LD node per artefact of a FHIR Implementation Guide, written from its artefact index beside the artefact's thin page (`artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld`): the FHIR RDF class, Dublin Core and schema.org identity, each representation as a `schema:MediaObject`, and PROV for a compiled copy. It is the asset a thin artefact page renders. Beside them, one index node (`artifact/index.jsonld`, `folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1`) lists every artefact in the Publisher's order, each entry naming its node: what the thin `artifacts` and `toc` pages draw.

avatar.reads: a card beside a JSON-LD brace — one IG artefact as a linked-data node

rationale: The owner, 2026-10-11, option A: IG artefact pages as "tiny html w/ dynamic load from json(ld) KG", with the JSON-LD WHO-free. A kind of its own rather than a family of `fhir-artifact-index`: the index is one document about the whole IG and is harvested or compiled, while these are one node per artefact, written from the index, and are what a browser fetches. `derived`: `ig-artifact-jsonld.ts` writes every node from the index and none is edited, so a finding against a node is a finding against the writer. Not `renderable`: the site build does not read the directory; the thin pages written beside the nodes (`gen-ig-pages.ts --thin`) render them. Vocabularies are borrowed (FHIR RDF classes, dcterms, schema.org, PROV) and nothing is minted; `schemas/ig-artifact-jsonld.ts` says which term says what. QA beyond shape is `ig-artifact-jsonld.ts check`: every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node's key, type and @id are its own file's, its `.json` twin matches, and every local resource it names is on the built site. The index node is the same kind, a second family: it is written from the same index by the same writer, summarises the nodes it names, and `check` holds each entry to its node (key and class) and the list to the index (every artefact once, the count stated).
